minutes.headline: Commission continued the Hickory Hills well pilot study hearing to June 21 over notice and drywell concerns; no approval.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission approved a Hickory Hills Lake herbicide plan, continued the town beach sand request, approved a Fire Road 19 rebuild and a septic repair, and heard a long contested hearing on the Lunenburg Water District's PFAS pilot study. That hearing was continued to June 21 so the applicant can supply a drywell schematic, an overflow plan, a remediation plan and securing details. Several other hearings were continued, and certificates of compliance and a tree removal were approved.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none offered.
Asked how plans are enforced if an owner builds beyond the approved plan; chair described certificates of completion and a roof ordered removed.

Read a statement for the Woodlands Village condominium saying it was not properly notified as an abutter of the water district pilot study and asking for postponement; later objected to the tanks, asked for soil testing for PFAS and presented sample data.
Asked about the pilot schedule, PFAS breakthrough testing, leak and freeze risk, and criticised the lack of notification to Woodlands residents.
Said a majority of direct abutters were not notified; asked about drywell depth and capacity, pilot duration and design.
Asked that the notice of intent be updated with specific details before any approval.
Raised the weight of the water tank and a hydrogeology report on lake levels.
Concerned about erosion and runoff to the lake near the tank and drywell.
Asked about alarm systems for malfunctions.
Asked about noise and whether test results would go to the commission.
Asked the engineer for a list of recent PFAS pilot study towns and for a schematic of the system.
Asked who is liable if something goes wrong.
Asked how truck traffic would affect wetlands.
Water district staff asked why they were not told about the site visit.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission continued the Lunenburg Water District's Hickory Hills well pilot study hearing to June 21 without approving it.
The hearing was contested: abutters, including a condominium association, said they were not properly notified, and raised drywell, tank, runoff and liability questions.
The chair and administrator will send the applicant a list of corrective actions and questions before June 21.
The commission approved the Hickory Hills Lake herbicide pre-treatment plan and a Fire Road 19 home rebuild with a new septic system.
The town beach sand hearing, the skatepark hearing and the Payne retaining walls hearing were each continued to June 21.

why_it_matters: The water district's PFAS pilot study stays unapproved until at least June 21, and the notice dispute with neighbors must be settled before the commission can act on it.
Residents near Hickory Hills Lake or the Woodlands can still raise concerns about the pilot's tanks, drainage and monitoring at the continued hearing.
watch_next: June 21 Conservation Commission meeting: continued hearings on the well pilot study, town beach sand, the skatepark and the Payne retaining walls.
The applicant's drywell schematic, overflow plan, remediation plan and securing details, due before the pilot study hearing resumes.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main approvals: the Hickory Hills pre-treatment plan, 20 Fire Road 19, the Jewell negative determination, 611 Reservoir Road and 147 Robs Hill Road. They differ on four votes to continue hearings to June 21, which only our minutes record, and on the chair's recusal at 17 Crocker Ave, which the official minutes do not mention. Three decisions are described differently or are one-sided, and several names were misheard in our captions.
